Macworld

Apple has had a busy fall, with the launch of the iPhone Duo, HomeView smart hub, and the M5 Ultra Mac Studio. But there’s one more event this week, and it might be the biggest of all. And you can follow every rumor and announcement with us right here.

As you can guess by the thinly veiled pun, this week’s marquee announcement is a new MacBook Pro, but not just any MacBook Pro. After years of denials, Apple appears to be on the verge of releasing its first-ever touchscreen MacBook. Rumors say it will have a new design with a lighter chassis, Dynamic Island, and an OLED display. And a very high price tag.

But first, Apple kicked off its week of releases on Monday with the new iPad mini, which got a thinner design, new A20 Pro chip, and an OLED display. Then on Tuesday, Apple announced a new iMac with a new M6 chip along with the M6 MacBook Pro. Neither new machine has much different other than the new chip and some faster networking protocols. But thankfully, the prices didn’t go up.

Pro and Tell event: Live blog

1 hour ago, By Michael Simon

What are you willing to pay?

We ran a poll on X asking users what they’d be willing to pay for a new 16-inch touchscreen MacBook Pro. The results were a somewhat expected, with more than 70 percent of responders saying they wouldn’t pay more than $3,000. Considering the current model starts at $2,999, we fully expact the new one to start at over $3,000. The good news for Apple is more than 20 percent would spend up to $4,000 and more than 5 percent are willing to part with more than $5,000 to get their fingers on the new machine. So get those Apple Cards ready.

5 hours ago, By Michael Simon

$400 touchscreen premium

On the eve of the llaunch of Apple’s first touchscreen MacBook, Mark Gurman reports that Apple has considered charging $400 more than the current non-touch models. That would mean the 16-inch M5 Pro touchscreen MacBook Pro would start at around $3,500, while the 14-inch model starts at under $3,000. That’s a lot, but not quite as much as we feared for an MacBook Pro with an OLED display. We’ll see what else the new laptops bring soon enough.

8 hours ago, By Michael Simon

Touchscreen interest?

We polled users on X to gauge the level of interest in a touchscreen MacBook Pro, and the results are somewhat surprising. More than half of the people who cared enough to respond are at least somewhat interested in what Apple brings to the tablet tomorrow. Check out the results below:

9 hours ago, By Michael Simon

Wallpaper shmallpaper

Ever since Apple has been releasing devices with screens, each generation has received new wallpaper to help distinguish between the old and new models. Except new Macs haven’t gotten new wallpaper for a while. Today’s MacBook Pro has the same wallpaper introduced with the M3 model back in 2023, while the iMac’s wallpaper is indistinguishable from the M4 model it replaces. Does that matter? Not really, but it also shows how little Apple thinks about these upgrades. A new MacBook Pro is supposed to launch tomorrow. I’ll be looking at the wallpaper.

Apple

13 hours ago, By Michael Simon

Later launch on Wednesday

If you look at the pre-order times for the new iPad mini, iMac and MacBook Pro, you’ll see that they start at 10:10 am PT tomorrow. That also lines up with Apple’s hands-on event happening in LA at 10 am PT. So you probably don’t need to wake up early tomorrow to get a look at the touchscreen MacBook Pro. I’m pretty sure it won’t pop up on Apple’s website until 10 am PT/1 pm PT.

13 hours ago, By Michael Simon

Apple's 'exciting' week isn't very exciting (yet)

After the iPhone Duo and Homeview, this final product launch of 2026 isn’t all that exciting, despite Greg Joswiak’s promise. At least not yet. Now that Apple has gotten the iPad mini, iMac, and MacBook Pro out of the way, the stage is set for the first-ever touchscreen MacBook Pro, which should bring a slew of exciting changes to Apple’s high-end laptop. Along with the touchscreen, there is expected to be a new design that’s much lighter, an upgraded hinge that doesn’t wobble when touched, and an OLED display. Now that’s exciting.

14 hours ago, By Michael Simon

Upgrade for Final Cut Pro users

In addition to the new iMac and MacBook Pro, Apple updated Creator Studio today with several new features, most notably building MotionVFX into Final Cut Pro. Apple purchased MotionVFX earlier this year, but the plugin remained a $29/month plugin. Now that’s free, “giving editors access to thousands of elements, including templates with unique themes, stylish graphics, titles, and transitions, as well as tools for rotoscoping, tracking, and color grading,” for the same price as before.

15 hours ago, By Michael Simon

Where are the new colors?

We’ve been reading reports about new iMac colors for years now, but they have yet to arrive. The new M6 models have the same seven “vibrant” colors: blue, purple, pink, orange, yellow, green, and silver. There’s nothing wrong with those options, but why would Apple test new colors but not release them? Anyway, here are your iMac options probably for the next 2-3 years:

15 hours ago, By Michael Simon

Faster Ethernet in the iMac

One small change in the iMac: The base model is now configurable up to 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet rather than 1 Gigabit Ethernet in the previous models. The four-port model comes with 2.5 Gigabit standard.

15 hours ago, By Michael Simon

Same MacBook Pro, new chip

Like the iMacs, the M6 MacBook Pro is identical to the M5 model, with a new chip and Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Otherwise you’re getting the exact same machine. But in these times, I’m thankful the price hasn’t increased.

15 hours ago, By Michael Simon

Just a new chip

The new iMac is very much the old iMac with a new chip. The colors, storage capacity, memory, display, and features are all the same. The only thing that’s improved is the wireless connectivity due to the N1 chip. Now you’ll get Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.

15 hours ago, By Michael Simon

Apple launches new M6 iMac and MacBook Pro

As expected, Apple has announced M6 upgrades to the MacBook Pro and iMac, with the same starting prices ($1,499 for the iMac and $1,999 for the MacBook Pro). I’m off to dive into the specs, but at first glance it seems to be a very minor update.

16 hours ago, By Michael Simon

How much will the new Macs cost?

Apple is expected to announce updates to the iMac and MacBook Pro this morning with new chips, possibly new colors, and probably a few other new features. But the question I have is, how much will they cost? Apple’s entry-level MacBook Pro already got a $300 bump in June, but Apple raised the price of the Mac mini, Apple TV 4K, and HomePod after their own bumps, so it’s possible the new M6 MacBook Pro crosses the $2,000.

The iMac currently starts at $1,499 with two Thunderbolt ports and a downgraded M4 with 8 cores, while the higher-end 10-core model with 4 Thunderbolt ports starts at $1,699. Both have 256GB hard drives. I wouldn’t be surprised to see the entry-level model axes and the storage increased to 1TB for a new starting price of $1,999.

16 hours ago, By David Price

The drawback of thinness

One of the many significant upgrades to the iPad mini announced yesterday was a redesign that sees the device drop from 6.3mm to 5.4mm thick. (It’s also shed 13 percent of its weight.) As my colleague Michael Simon pointed out yesterday, that puts the mini in the same ultra-slim company as the iPhone Air, unfolded iPhone Duo, and iPad Pro.

But of course there are drawbacks to this slimming down–and I’m not talking about lower battery life (which we’ll certainly test) or a tendency to bend (which other people who don’t mind damaging their loan units will certainly test). I’m talking about case compatibility.

Apple has added a new product to its online store called Smart Folio for iPad mini (A20 Pro). This accessory is certified as compatible with that model and no other. Will your existing cases work on the new iPad mini? Maybe (considering that the length and width are almost identical, and that many iPad cases attach on the back rather than completely enclosing the device), and maybe not. Best to give Apple $79 just to be on the safe side. Don’t complain. It’s thinner.

17 hours ago, By David Price

M6: What's the big deal?

Assuming today goes the way we expect, the next set of announcements will focus heavily on the upgrades delivered by the M6 processor. This is part of Apple’s latest chip generation, and made its first appearance, to critical acclaim, in the Mac mini in August. So what’s the big deal?

The key factor here is that the M6 is the first of Apple’s chips to use the new 2nm manufacturing process from TSMC, which allows the company to increase core counts and add features while making the chip smaller than the M5. It also lets the chip run at lower power and higher clock speeds. Today’s new iMac and MacBook Pro could be looking at both greater processing muscle and improved power efficiency, and that’s a killer combination by anyone’s standards.

If you want all the details about this exciting new chip and the benefits it brings, Macworld’s Jason Cross spent some time doing a thorough M6 deep dive.

18 hours ago, By David Price

Welcome to day two!

Good morning to European readers, and U.S. readers who’ve got out of bed commendably early. It’s day two of Apple’s Pro and Tell week of announcements.

Yesterday was all about the iPad. Today we’re expecting some Mac news: new M6 versions of the iMac and MacBook Pro. Based on yesterday the announcement is likely to happen at 9 am ET, 1 pm ET. Stay tuned!

1 day ago, By Michael Simon

Take our poll!

With two more days of announcements coming this week, we want to know what you’re planning to buy: an iPad mini, M6 iMac, M6 MacBook Pro, or touchscreen MacBook Pro. Readers are weighing in and there’s no surprise here, with 41 percent of the vote, the touchscreen MacBook Pro leads the pack. Join the conversation and take our poll online.

Spotlight on hinges

Following this weekend’s iPhone Duo hinge issues, which have led to numerous cracked and damaged screens, Mark Gurman reports that Apple will be putting emphasis on the MacBook Pro’s new hinge when the touchscreen model arrives this week. He says Apple has made it “more stable so touching the screen doesn’t make it rock during usage.” It’s just a good thing that the new laptop won’t involve folding glass.

1 day ago, By Michael Simon

OS 27.2 updates are out

Ahead of a round of new product releases this week, as well as the HomePod mini coming Friday and the 4th-gen Apple TV 4K coming next month, Apple has released its first major update to OS 27 for iPhones, iPads, Macs, and everything else. So even if you’re not planning on buying something new this week, you devices can get some new features at least.

1 day ago, By Michael Simon

Next up: Macs and more Macs!

We’re still expecting three more announcements this week: the M6 iMac, the M6 entry-level MacBook Pro, and the touchscreen MacBook Pro. We assume tomorrow will bring the updates to the iMac and MacBook Pro and Wednesday will cap the announcements with the touchscreen model. It’s going to be a fun week!

2 days ago, By Michael Simon

Assuming today goes the way we expect, the next set of announcements will focus heavily on the upgrades delivered by the M6 processor. This is part of Apple’s latest chip generation, and made its first appearance, to critical acclaim, in the Mac mini in August. So what’s the big deal?

There was no event, no livestream, no video presentation; just a press release and an update to Apple’s website. But as low-key, start-of-the-week product refreshes go, the 8th-gen iPad mini announcement was oddly impressive.

It has a much faster processor, jumping three generations from A17 Pro to A20 Pro. (Great news for those AI applications we all love so much.) It has a much better screen, going from LED to OLED with its deeper blacks and overall better color reproduction, while also becoming slightly larger (8.5 inches vs 8.3 inches) and considerably brighter (1,200 nits for HDR content vs 500 nits max). And the iPad itself has shrunk significantly in both thickness (6.3mm to 5.4mm) and weight (263 grams vs 297 grams), making it by far the most portable iPad yet.

Part of me applauds a valiant attempt to keep the iPad mini relevant instead of killing it off, as has seemed plausible at various stages in the product’s history. But another part thinks Apple has just responded to competition from the automobile industry by building the world’s fanciest horse and cart.

As I discussed briefly in our live blog for this week’s Apple announcements, the iPad mini’s great problem is that the ground has moved beneath its feet. When the device came out, an argument could be made that it was the best way for Apple fans to view movies and play games on the go. It was relatively cheap, portable, powerful, and above all delivered an experience you couldn’t get with any other Apple product. But that hasn’t been the case for some time now.

Apple

Take the phablet, as we used to call very large smartphones before products of that form factor became normal and even expected. They threaten mini tablets because they approach the same problem in a more versatile way. Yes, an iPad mini is cheaper than an iPhone 18 Pro Max. But the latter is also a phone. It’s more portable, more powerful, offers a very respectable 6.9-inch screen that’s great for games and movies, and it’s the only mobile device you need. Why buy an iPad mini and a phone when you can get both in one package?

But this year the iPad mini’s situation became even more desperate with the launch of the iPhone Duo. The Duo has its issues, but beating any iPad mini in a head-to-head is not one of them. It’s just straight up better: infinitely more portable in its folded form, very nearly as large-screened when unfolded, and vastly more powerful and versatile. A world containing the iPhone Duo is not one that’s friendly to the iPad mini, which is essentially a Duo you can’t close.

Does the A20 Pro update change the equation in any meaningful way? Thinness is always nice, the mini needed an up-to-date processor for future-proofing if nothing else, and the OLED screen is the sort of quality-of-life upgrade you can market around. But it’s still fundamentally a product whose niche got swallowed up by something more exciting. It still feels kind of obsolete. It’s still a knife at a gunfight.

Can the iPad mini succeed? I think so. But my advice, perhaps counterintuitively, would be for Apple to embrace the qualities and characteristics that make it different from the bigger iPhones and the more powerful iPads. It needs to be cheaper, not thinner. It needs to be tougher, not more powerful. (The new model’s water and dust resistance is a bigger deal, in my opinion.) It needs to become the iPad equivalent of the old iPhone SE, by delivering an old-fashioned experience for the niche audience that doesn’t want the newer and more expensive version.

The iPad mini can find a role if it focuses on going to the places where you wouldn’t take an iPhone Duo, and doing the jobs that aren’t suitable for an iPad Air. I want it to be an extremely convenient ebook reader and web surfer that’s equally at home by the pool or on the coffee table, not yet another identikit reworking of the iPhone-iPad continuum that doesn’t make as much sense as the alternatives on either side.

The iPad mini isn’t going to beat the iPhone Duo by being better: the horse isn’t going to run faster than a car, and the cart isn’t going to offer more comfortable seats. It’s not going to do the same jobs to the same standard. But the mini is different, and it can still succeed if Apple embraces that.

On Tuesday, Apple announced new features in the apps for Apple Creator Studio, its collection of professional creative apps for Mac, iPhone, and iPad. The updates will be available in November for free to current Creator Studio subscribers. Each of the 10 apps that make up Creator Studio received a major update.

Video software updates

Apple acquired plug-in developer MotionVFX earlier this year; the company specialized in video editing and graphics tools subscriptions that cost for $29 per month. The MotionVFX tools for color grading, rotoscoping, and tracking, as well as graphics, themed templates, titles, and transitions will be incorporated into Final Cut Pro in the update for no extra charge.

Final Cut Pro now has cross-app functionality with Pixelmator Pro, so editors can open images directly from the timeline and save changes back to the project without needing to reimport the image. Other enhancements include more keyframe easing options, the ability to disconnect clips from the primary storyline to place them anywhere on the timeline, and 23 new transcription languages.

Apple

Motion also benefits from the MotionVFX acquisition; it incorporates new options for 3D camera tracking, cinematic color grading, and one-click selection for visual effects. Motion also supports a new Displacement filter, image generation and edits from text descriptions, cross-app functionality with Pixelmator Pro, and fine-tuned keyframe easing. Compressor supports the ability to encode Cinematic mode video recorded on iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo.

Pixelmator Pro

Pixelmator Pro gets the power of AI with its new Generate Fill option that performs edits based on a user’s description. It takes into account the surrounding area to match lighting, perspective, and texture to create a seamless blend. Sharpness is maintained with Pixelmator Pro’s built-in Super Resolution technology.

Logic Pro

Apple worked with OpenAI for a new intelligent assistant in Logic Pro for Mac. The assistant can be used for navigating workflow productions, refining an active project, starting a new song, or setting up a vocal track. The Browser has been redesigned to make it easier to find effect patches, instruments, loops, and more. Logic Pro can analyze and classify sounds to make them easier to find.

The enhanced Stem Splitter now has the ability to isolate, replace, or rebalance drum parts without needing the original multitracks. A new Sergio George Producer Pack features authentic Latin jazz and salsa loops, including a full salsa percussion section, brass ensemble, and basses.

Apple

Logic Pro also has a Voice Memo Studio Sound feature that can reduce noise in iPhone recordings. And Logic Pro on both the Mac and iPad has Liquid Glass Ui enhancements.

Freeform, Keynote, Numbers, Pages

Apple’s productivity apps are enhanced by a new “Intelligent Assistant” that understands document context and can be used to develop content. For example, the assistant in Keynote can be used to design slides. In Pages, the assistant can help with fine-tuning what’s been written. In Numbers, the assistant can calculate, visualize, and organize data, recommend chart types, and build custom tables. Apple accidentally revealed these features last week when it prematurely posted the update.

The Content Hub for these apps now includes Apple-curated stock video footage, and subscribers get new templates and themes. Keynote introduces support for Keynote Interchange Format (.keyx), an open JSON-based bundle file format. Freeform adds text styles, and in December, will have the ability to edit images directly in Pixelmator Pro and generate editable shapes from text descriptions.

Apple Creator Studio is available via subscription for $12.99/£12.99 per month or $129/£129 per year. Education pricing is available. Up to six family members can share all of the apps and content included in Apple Creator Studio with Family Sharing. One-time-purchase versions of Final Cut Pro, Logic Pro, Pixelmator Pro, Motion, Compressor, and MainStage are available on the Mac App Store. Freeform, Keynote, Numbers, and Pages are free.

Apple has updated the iMac with its M6 chip, bringing faster processing, stronger graphics, and improved AI capabilities to its colorful all-in-one desktop. Announced on October 27, 2026, the new model replaces the M4 iMac introduced in 2024, with Apple skipping the M5 generation.

The five biggest upgrades are faster CPU performance, more powerful graphics, improved AI processing, faster SSD storage, and upgraded networking. Both configurations gain additional CPU and GPU cores, a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and greater memory bandwidth.

Connectivity improves with Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and available 2.5Gb Ethernet. However, the familiar 24-inch design remains, along with the seven color options, 4.5K Retina display, and 12MP Center Stage camera. Starting memory and storage are unchanged at 16GB and 256GB.

The M6 iMac starts at $1,499 for the two-port model and $1,699 for the four-port version. Preorders open October 28, with deliveries and store availability beginning November 6.

M6 vs. M4 iMac: The biggest changes

The upgrades differ slightly depending on whether you choose the two-port or four-port model.

Apple announced the M6 iMac on October 27, 2026. Preorders open on Wednesday, October 28, at:

  • 1:10 p.m. Eastern
  • 5:10 p.m. GMT

The new iMac will begin arriving with customers on Friday, November 6, when it also becomes available in Apple Stores and through Apple Authorized Resellers. Customers can preorder through Apple’s website or the Apple Store app.

M6 iMac design: What has changed?

Apple

The M6 iMac retains the slim, colorful design introduced with the M1 model in 2021. It has white display bezels, a colored chin beneath the screen, and a matching stand. There is no notch.

Apple continues to offer seven finishes: blue, green, pink, orange, yellow, purple, and silver. Despite pre-launch speculation about new colors, Apple has not announced any new color options.

Dimensions and weights are unchanged from the equivalent M4 models:

Keyboard and mouse

Apple

Both models retain color-matched Magic accessories. The two-port model includes a Magic Keyboard with a Lock key. Buyers can configure it with a Magic Keyboard featuring Touch ID and a numeric keypad. The four-port model includes a Touch ID keyboard, with a numeric-keypad version available as an option.

Both configurations offer a Magic Mouse or an optional Magic Trackpad. USB-C charging for these accessories carries over from the M4 generation.

M6 iMac display: Is the screen better?

Apple

The display specifications are unchanged. Both models have a 24-inch LED-backlit 4.5K Retina display, with an actual diagonal measurement of 23.5 inches.

Nano-texture glass remains an option for reducing reflections in bright environments.

The camera and audio specifications also carry over: a 12MP Center Stage camera with Desk View and 1080p video recording, a six-speaker system with force-cancelling woofers, Dolby Atmos Spatial Audio, and a three-microphone array.

M6 iMac processor: How much faster is it?

Apple

The M6 is manufactured using a 2-nanometer process, replacing the second-generation 3nm technology used for M4. The smaller process increases transistor density and helps improve performance and power efficiency.

CPU and graphics

The two-port iMac moves from an eight-core CPU and GPU to ten cores of each. That is a 25 percent increase in core counts.

The four-port model moves from a ten-core CPU and GPU to twelve cores of each—a 20 percent increase. That’s more cores, not necessarily a measured speed improvements.

Both M6 configurations introduce two super cores. The entry model pairs these with three performance cores and five efficiency cores; the four-port version has four performance cores and six efficiency cores.

Neural Engine and AI processing

Both configurations gain a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, replacing M4’s single 16-core engine. Neural Accelerators in the GPU add further processing capability for supported AI workloads.

Memory bandwidth for both M6 models increases from 120GB/s to as much as 170GB/s—approximately 42 percent higher.

Apple’s performance claims

Apple identifies a 10-core M4 with 32GB memory and a 2TB SSD as its previous-generation comparison configuration.

Media engine

Apple lists the same media-format capabilities across both generations: hardware acceleration for H.264, HEVC, ProRes, and ProRes RAW, plus AV1 decoding.

M6 iMac RAM: How much memory does it have?

Memory capacities are unchanged:

The main change is faster access to memory, rather than more included RAM.

For everyday browsing, office applications, and family use, 16GB should be sufficient. Buyers working with larger creative projects or demanding multitasking should consider 24GB. The four-port model’s 32GB option offers more headroom for memory-intensive applications and larger local AI models.

Unified memory is shared by the CPU, GPU, and other components. More capacity lets applications and local models hold more data in memory, potentially reducing reliance on SSD swap.

M6 iMac connectivity: What’s new?

Apple

Both models upgrade from Wi-Fi 6E to Wi-Fi 7 and from Bluetooth 5.3 to Bluetooth 6.

Ethernet improves too. Apple’s comparison documents list optional 2.5Gb Ethernet on the two-port M6 model and include it as standard on the four-port version. Their M4 equivalents offered optional and standard Gigabit Ethernet, respectively.

The higher Ethernet connection speed can benefit transfers to compatible network storage, but requires suitable network equipment.

Apple also lists its N1 wireless networking chip and Thread support.

Port counts remain unchanged: two Thunderbolt/USB 4 ports on the entry model and four Thunderbolt 4 ports on the higher version. The 3.5mm headphone socket retains support for high-impedance headphones.

The color-matched magnetic 143W power adapter connector remains.

M6 iMac price: How much will it cost?

The M6 iMac starts at $1,499 for the two-port model and $1,699 for the four-port model, both with 16GB memory and a 256GB SSD.

Those prices match the outgoing M4 prices, but they are $200 higher than the M4’s original 2024 launch prices, which Apple increased in June 2026.


The entry-level storage remains 256GB. The two-port model can be configured with 512GB or 1TB; the four-port model adds a 2TB option. These capacities match the M4 iMac.

Should you buy the M6 iMac?

The M6 iMac is the most compelling for buyers replacing an older Intel iMac or seeking an integrated desktop with a display, camera, speakers, keyboard, and mouse.

M4 owners have less reason to upgrade unless a particular workload is already limiting them. The screen, camera, audio hardware, memory capacities, and overall design remain familiar. Independent testing will establish how much difference M6 makes in everyday use.

Which model should you buy?

Choose the two-port model for everyday home computing, schoolwork, browsing, and office applications. It receives the headline Neural Engine and memory-bandwidth improvements, so buyers do not need the four-port model simply to obtain those upgrades.

Choose the four-port model for its faster 12-core CPU and GPU, additional connections, included Ethernet, and Touch ID keyboard. It also supports 32GB memory and 2TB storage configurations.

For a flexible home-office or creative setup, our provisional recommendation is the four-port model with 24GB memory and a 512GB SSD, subject to upgrade pricing. Buyers running larger local AI models should assess whether the 32GB option meets their software’s requirements.

A substantially discounted M4 remains worth considering for everyday use. Compare equivalent memory, storage, and port configurations when judging the saving.

Apple today announced an M6 update to its iMac desktop line, heralding “a major boost in performance and AI capabilities.” But other than the upgrade from an M4 to an M6 chip there’s little change from the previous model.

Admittedly that chip upgrade, leaping two generations in a single refresh, is a significant one. Apple claims the M6 will deliver up to 1.5x faster performance than M4 in apps such as Excel, up to 2x faster graphics performance, and up to 2x higher gaming performance with ray tracing. AI, inevitably, is foregrounded too, with Apple claiming the M6 is capable of up to 5x faster on-device AI prompt processing in LM Studio. This could be a worthwhile upgrade if performance in these categories is a bottleneck for you.

There are also some connectivity improvements. Wi-Fi has been bumped from version 6E (802.11ax) to 7 (802.11be), and Bluetooth from 5.3 to 6. Gigabit Ethernet on the M4 model has been upgraded to 2.5Gb Ethernet here. And Apple claims the new iMac offers up to 2x faster SSD read and write, which means “apps launch quickly, and large files like photo libraries and video projects load in an instant.” Macworld will put all this to the test when we get hold of a review sample, of course, but we’ve seen what Apple’s done with SSD speeds this year and are inclined to believe the claims.

Apple

Beyond that, however, there’s not much to say. The opening section of the press release promises “blazing-fast performance, enhanced connectivity, Siri AI, and macOS 27, all in a stunning design in seven vibrant colors.” The first two I’ve already discussed. It’s not a good sign when a company has to fall back on old features that early in a new product’s announcement.

Even the camera and speaker setups are unchanged, and you get the same number of ports: either two or four USB 4, depending on which model you pick, plus a 3.5mm headphone jack.

We loved the iMac M4, which our reviewer said “might be the best iMac ever.” And there’s a lot to like about the M6 chip refresh. So this is unlikely to be a bad product. After weeks of development with enrolled beta testers, iOS 27.2 is available to all iPhone users as a stable release, along with macOS, iPadOS, watchOS, and tvOS. The first major update to iOS 27 introduces several handy enhancements to Siri AI, along with some major additions to Apple TV and HomePod.

What happened to iOS 27.1?

It’s odd for Apple to jump from iOS 27.0.1 to iOS 27.2, but there’s a simple explanation: iOS 27.1 was strictly for the iPhone Duo. There was never a developer or public beta release, but Apple likely had a similar program for the software in-house as to not leak specific features for the folding phone. In fact, iPhone Duo users had to update to a newer build of iOS 27.1 after unboxing their phones. 

iOS 27.2 is compatible with all iPhones, including the Duo, so iOS 27.1 might go down as the shortest-lived update Apple has ever released.

Siri AI expansion

Siri AI first launched with iOS 27.0, unlocking a comprehensive chatbot experience in a dedicated app—plus the ability to recall personal data and take in-app action. The initial version, however, was limited to a single language. While the assistant could comprehend many languages when texting it, its main interface and voice commands only supported English. With iOS 27.2, Siri AI officially expands language support to include French, Spanish, Portuguese, Japanese, and Korean.

The latest update also expands what Siri AI can do in Apple’s native communication apps. In Messages, Siri now suggests relevant actions under individual texts when needed. For example, if someone mentions a date, the assistant will surface a shortcut to quickly add it to the Calendar app. Meanwhile, the Phone app’s Call Context feature now highlights saved anniversaries, a welcome addition to the existing birthday reminders.

Another new feature is Siri’s ability to reference previous queries. Siri will now be able to access prior chats even when not continuing a conversation in the Siri app.

iOS 27.2 should also expand Siri AI’s platform availability, unlocking it on the second-generation Apple TV 4K and newer models. Once you install the latest iOS and tvOS builds, your Apple TV 4K will rely on your nearby iPhone to handle personal requests on the big screen. It’s worth noting, however, that Siri AI has yet to be activated on the tvOS 27.2 Release Candidate at the time of writing, and since the new Apple TV doesn’t release until November 13, it may require a separate update.

Mahmoud Itani/Foundry

Apple TV profiles

Speaking of Apple TV, iOS 27.2 brings a highly requested feature to the streaming service. Similar to Netflix, the TV app on your iPhone now allows you to create multiple viewer profiles tied to a single Apple Account.

If you tend to share your personal iPhone or iPad with a family member, they will be able to use your subscription to watch original movies and series without altering your queue or watch history. This does not impact the existing Family Sharing perk that allows up to six independent Apple Accounts to take advantage of a single subscription on their own devices.

Some of the features supported by Apple TV profiles include picking a name and avatar, restricting adult content, adding a 4-digit PIN, and setting autoplay defaults. Notably, the primary account holder will be able to view, manage, and delete any of the secondary profiles created using their account.

Sound Glow on HomePods

The latest OS update revitalizes all HomePod models except the original full-size model from 2018. Once you install iOS and HomePod Software 27.2, you’ll be able to toggle a new Sound Glow setting in the iPhone’s built-in Home app. 

The feature distills a playing song’s album art into a color blob that animates on the HomePod’s top display in sync with the rhythm. While Sound Glow doesn’t affect the actual audio, it does make vibing to music more fun—especially in pitch-black environments, which amplify the dramatic effect.

Other handy HomePod options in the OS 27.2 release include a Lock Controls toggle that disables the touchscreen. If your smart speaker suffers from ghost touch issues, you’ll be able to make it usable again by turning off touch input. 

Mahmoud Itani/Foundry

App Switcher on watchOS

After updating your iPhone, you’ll want to install watchOS 27.2 on your Apple Watch. This release brings back the App Switcher on watchOS after version 27.0 removed it, making it possible to force-quit misbehaving apps again.

It’s not as simple as before, however. Instead of double-clicking the Digital Crown, you’ll now have to tap and hold on the bottom of the screen inside an app to reveal the App Switcher. The retired mechanism will be reassigned to the Apple Watch Series 12’s Live Rewind feature when it debuts later this year.

Mahmoud Itani/Foundry

Apple Pencil support for iPhone Duo

What happened to iOS 27.1?

It’s odd for Apple to jump from iOS 27.0.1 to iOS 27.2, but there’s a simple explanation: iOS 27.1 was strictly for the iPhone Duo. There was never a developer or public beta release, but Apple likely had a similar program for the software in-house as to not leak specific features for the folding phone. In fact, iPhone Duo users had to update to a newer build of iOS 27.1 after unboxing their phones. 

iOS 27.2 is compatible with all iPhones, including the Duo, so iOS 27.1 might go down as the shortest-lived update Apple has ever released.

Siri AI expansion

Siri AI first launched with iOS 27.0, unlocking a comprehensive chatbot experience in a dedicated app—plus the ability to recall personal data and take in-app action. The initial version, however, was limited to a single language. While the assistant could comprehend many languages when texting it, its main interface and voice commands only supported English. With iOS 27.2, Siri AI officially expands language support to include French, Spanish, Portuguese, Japanese, and Korean.

The latest update also expands what Siri AI can do in Apple’s native communication apps. In Messages, Siri now suggests relevant actions under individual texts when needed. For example, if someone mentions a date, the assistant will surface a shortcut to quickly add it to the Calendar app. Meanwhile, the Phone app’s Call Context feature now highlights saved anniversaries, a welcome addition to the existing birthday reminders.

Another new feature is Siri’s ability to reference previous queries. Siri will now be able to access prior chats even when not continuing a conversation in the Siri app.

This does not impact the existing Family Sharing perk that allows up to six independent Apple Accounts to take advantage of a single subscription on their own devices.
